title: Recording: Mary Had A Little Lamb by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio Two, Island Studios, London
Producer: Glyn Johns
Engineers: Phil Ault

Paul McCartney continued recording Wings’ second single, ‘Mary Had A Little Lamb’, on 1 April 1972.

The session marked an unexpected return for producer Glyn Johns, who had walked away from recording Wings on 29 March. Keen to play the pipes of peace, he called McCartney and offered to complete the recording.

Olympic Studios was unavailable at the weekend, so McCartney and Johns went instead to Island Studios in London. Joining them were Linda McCartney and daughters Heather and Mary.

‘Mary Had A Little Lamb’ was mostly complete, and mainly required vocals. Paul taped his lead vocals on this day, joined in places by Linda. He then double-tracked his part, adding harmonies in places.

We were overdubbing mainly vocals, and everything was relaxed and workmanlike. When it was lunchtime, I stumped up the £10 for us all to eat, as they hadn’t any cash. Two days later a cab arrived at Basing Street with £10 in an envelope for me, which I was impressed with – the mark of a true gent!
Phil Ault, engineer, 23 September 2021
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73, Allan Kozinn, Adrian Sinclair
Page last updated: 20 November 2025
